takeaways.label: Strong top line, margin squeeze
takeaways.text: Consolidated revenue grew 30% YoY to ₹496.3 crores, but EBITDA margin compressed to 14.6% as API cost increases could not be passed through swiftly enough in export markets.

takeaways.label: Jammu facility is the growth engine
takeaways.text: The plant hit a ₹450 crore annualized run-rate, completed marquee customer audits, and is expected to accelerate to ₹140–150 crores per quarter in the near term.

takeaways.label: Export pass-through lag is the margin culprit
takeaways.text: A 2.8% consolidated gross margin hit stemmed from longer-duration international purchase orders that delay pricing transfers, while standalone margins saw only a 0.8% impact because shorter cycles allow swifter adjustment.

takeaways.label: 20% volume growth model intact for two years
takeaways.text: Management sees existing efforts sustaining the trajectory through FY29, with a ₹400 crore treasury available for greenfield or inorganic moves to fuel growth beyond that.

watch.label: What to watch next quarter
watch.text: Whether API prices stabilize so margins normalize, the pace of Jammu’s ramp toward the ₹500 crore annual target, and any tangible signal on the acquisition pipeline for post-FY29 growth.

points.label: Production milestone
points.text: The facility started production in January 2025 and has now completed six quarters of operations, reaching an annualized revenue base of ₹450 crores.

points.label: Customer validation done
points.text: Key marquee customer audits were successfully completed and onboarding of those customers is now finished, setting the stage for accelerated revenue in coming quarters.

points.label: Near-term trajectory
points.text: Revenue is expected in the ₹140–150 crores per quarter range over the next two quarters, up from ₹105 crores this quarter.

points.label: Runway
points.text: The facility has roughly two years of room to grow, with a potential to reach ₹1,200–1,300 crores.

points.label: Margin contribution
points.text: Jammu contributed EBITDA of around ₹2 crores to ₹2.25 crores this quarter, still in early-stage ramp.

points.label: The core problem
points.text: Consolidated gross margin was impacted by 2.8%, while standalone gross margin saw only a 0.8% hit, because domestic purchase order cycles are shorter and pricing transfers happen faster than in export markets.

points.label: No retrospective relief
points.text: Price adjustments from customers for API increases are always on a prospective, PO-to-PO basis; retrospective adjustments normally do not happen.

points.label: Contractual protection exists
points.text: API price movements are contractually built to be passed through to customers on a long-term basis, so the margin hit is a timing issue, not a permanent loss.

points.label: Normalization path
points.text: If API prices stabilize, margins should move back to a normalized position; management reiterated the margin will stay within a plus/minus 2% range and improvement will be organic and gradual.

points.label: Ex-Jammu organic growth
points.text: The ex-Jammu portfolio (Innova, Univentis, Sharon) is growing organically at 10%–12% with margin consolidation and revenue ramp-up.

points.label: ROE math
points.text: With 3x FATR and 15%–16% EBITDA margin, the business model yields 16%–17% ROE with 90 days of working capital; any improvement in EBITDA margin can lift ROE to 20%.

points.label: Beyond FY29
points.text: The company is evaluating both greenfield and inorganic acquisition opportunities to trigger growth beyond FY29, with a treasury of around ₹400 crores available for reinvestment and healthy debt equity.

points.label: CDMO and branded generics
points.text: CDMO revenue grew 30% YoY in Q2 and branded generic revenue grew 32% YoY; exports contributed 29% of Q2 revenue.

rows: Deploy ~₹400 crore treasury into greenfield or inorganic acquisition
When a tangible conclusion is reached

items.title: Jammu facility ramp-up
items.text: Kathua's four-block greenfield plant (₹480+ cr capex) exited FY26 at a ₹90 cr quarterly run rate, hit ₹107 cr in Q1 FY27, and turned EBITDA-positive. Management targets ₹1,000 cr+ revenue from this facility in 2-3 years against ~25-30% utilization today - roughly 3x current total revenue if achieved.

items.title: Baddi general block expansion
items.text: Land acquired August 2025 for a new oral tablet/capsule and liquid facility, with capex estimated at ₹150-170 cr across FY27-FY28. At optimum level this block alone could add ₹450-500 cr revenue, relieving the capacity constraints currently capping the general portfolio.

items.title: Branded generics scale-up
items.text: Q1 FY27 branded generics revenue grew 39% YoY to ₹142.2 cr, following FY26's 51% jump to ₹497 cr. The business runs at ~70% domestic trade generics with 2,50,000+ touchpoints, and management is pushing into new geographies and products - the fastest-growing segment at roughly double the CDMO growth rate.

items.title: CDMO wallet-share expansion
items.text: CDMO revenue grew 32% YoY in Q1 FY27 to ₹328.7 cr, driven by new customers and higher wallet share from existing ones. With 350+ clients across 60+ countries and ~80% of revenue from partners served over 5 years, the model compounds through repeat orders and new contract wins without needing new capacity.

items.title: Sharon Bio-Medicine integration
items.text: Sharon (acquired June 2023) contributed ~₹240 cr revenue in FY26 with margins above company average, and is expected to grow in early teens organically. Its Dehradun and Taloja plants run at 60-70% utilization with room to 70-80%, and it opens regulated markets (Canada, UK, Europe, Australia) that the parent couldn't reach alone.

items.title: Regulatory approvals opening regulated markets
items.text: UK-MHRA approved the Baddi cephalosporin plant and PIC/S (SMDC Ukraine) certified the Kathua, Jammu facility in FY26. These certifications unlock sales into UK, Canada, and other regulated markets - exports already rose from 25.9% of revenue in FY25 to 31.3% in FY26.

items.title: Jammu GST incentive
items.text: The facility qualifies for GST-linked incentives totaling 300% of eligible plant and machinery investment over 10 years, plus 6% annual interest subvention on term loans. The GST rate cut on formulations (12% to 5%) means the full ~₹75-80 cr incentive now requires ~₹1,400 cr annual sales - which aligns with the facility's peak revenue potential.

items.title: Semaglutide and GLP-1 development
items.text: R&D work on semaglutide is underway with positive initial results, targeting a "wave 2" launch after the 2026 patent expiry of GLP-1 drugs. This is a high-value CDMO opportunity that could add a new revenue leg if the company captures even a small share of the generic wave.
